sanskrit: sahasrārghaḥ śatakāṇḍaḥ payasvān apām agnir vīrudhāṃ rājasūyam | sa no 'yaṃ darbhaḥ pari pātu viśvato daivo maṇir āyuṣā saṃ sṛjāti naḥ ||
english: Worth a thousand, hundred-stalked, full of sap, the fire of waters among plants, the royal-consecration among herbs — may this darbha grass of ours, this divine amulet, protect us on every side and unite us with long life.

sanskrit: ghṛtād ullupto madhumān payasvān bhūmidṛṃho acyutaś cāvayiṣṇuḥ | nudan sapatnān adharāṃś ca kṛṇvan darbhāroha mahatā mahendriyeṇa ||
english: Anointed with ghee, sweet with honey, full of milk, fast-rooted in the earth, immovable and yet inclining — thrusting rivals down and making them inferior, ascend, O Darbha, with great and mighty virile power.

sanskrit: tvaṃ bhūmim aty eṣy ojasā tvaṃ vedyāṃ sīdasi cārur adhvare | tvāṃ pavitram ṛṣayo 'bharanta tvaṃ punīhi duritāny asmat ||
english: You traverse the earth with vigor; you sit beautifully upon the vedi at the sacrifice; the seers carried you as a purifier — do you purify from us all the things that go wrong.

sanskrit: tīkṣṇo rājā viṣāsahī rakṣohā viśvacarṣaṇiḥ | tejo devānāṃ balam ugram etat taṃ te badhnāmi jarase svastaye ||
english: Sharp king, conqueror of poison, slayer of rākṣasas, beholder of all creatures — this is the fiery splendor and the fierce strength of the gods; that I bind upon you for old age and for well-being.

sanskrit: darbheṇa tvaṃ kṛṇu vīryāṇi darbhaṃ bibhrad ātmanā mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ | atiṣṭhāyo varcasaidhvanyān sūrya ivā bhāhi pradiśaś catasraḥ ||
english: With darbha, accomplish heroic deeds; bearing darbha, do not tremble within yourself; stand pre-eminent — grow bright in glory above others; shine like the sun upon the four quarters.

sanskrit: ud īratāṃ pṛthivī jīradānuḥ śīta enām antarvān anu vātu vātaḥ | ṛtviyāvatī pṛthivī prati gṛhṇātu bījaṃ sahasravalliśaṃ suruhārohayantī ||
english: Let the earth, the giver of sustenance, be stirred up; let the cold wind, bearing rain within, blow upon her; let the seasonally endowed earth receive the seed — she who causes good plants to spring up, yielding a thousandfold growth.

sanskrit: indra enāṃ haryaśvo agnir vā rohitāśvaḥ | aśvinā rāsabhāśvā kṛṣiṃ devīm ayūyujan ||
english: Indra with his bay horses, or Agni with his red horses, and the Aśvins with their ass-and-horse team — they have yoked the divine field.

sanskrit: śunaṃ varatrām ā yaccha śunam aṣṭrām ud iṅgaya | śunaṃ totapyatāṃ phālaḥ śunaṃ vahatu lāṅgalam ||
english: Draw the yoke-strap auspiciously; auspiciously raise the goad; auspiciously let the ploughshare cut; auspiciously let the plough be drawn.

sanskrit: yunaktu vāhān vi yugā tanota kṛte kṣetre vapateha bījam | tathā dhātā tathā bhagas tathā kṛṇutām aśvinā tathā devī sarasvatī ||
english: Yoke the draft animals, stretch the yoke-ropes wide; in the prepared field sow the seed here. So too may Dhātṛ, so may Bhaga, so may the Aśvins accomplish it, so may the goddess Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: supippalā oṣadhayo nāhīnā apakṣata | tad indro varuṇo vāyur aśvinedaṃ me pra tiratā vacaḥ ||
english: May the herbs be richly berried, neither stripped of berries nor fallen away. Indra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Aśvins — extend this my word of mine.

sanskrit: dhātā pūṣā bṛhaspatir bhūtyāḥ sam ajīgaman | kṛṣiṃ devāḥ svarvidaḥ ||
english: Dhātṛ, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati — they have come together for prosperity; the gods who know the way to heaven have come to the field.

sanskrit: kalyāṇī subhageva yā saṃsthāyāṃ vapuṣeṇyā | sā nas tirāti madhumantam aṃśum ||
english: She who is auspicious, like fair fortune, desirable in form at the place of establishment — may she draw forth for us the sweet-flowing sap.

sanskrit: annasya bhūmā puruṣasya bhūmā bhūmā paśūnāṃ ta iha śrayantām | tīvrā varṣantu vṛṣṭayo bhūtaye mahase vṛdhe ||
english: Abundance of food, abundance of men, abundance of cattle — may these take up their abode here; let the rains rain fiercely for existence, for greatness, for growth.

sanskrit: pinvānaḥ parjanyas tiṣṭhatu saha pṛṣṭhayod eti sūryaḥ | ānandaṃ janayan yavaḥ sarvā arātīr apabādhamānaḥ ||
english: Let Parjanya stand swelling with the ridge-waters; the sun goes forth; barley generating joy, driving away all grudging niggardliness.

sanskrit: vi jihīṣva pṛthivīm ahyur vi pakṣam ṛdvī bhava | bhadraṃ rohatu dhānyam ||
english: Open wide the earth, O snake; be split apart with your wing — be propitious; let the grain sprout auspiciously.

sanskrit: utsedha sedha gā ajan vindeherāṃ mahas kṛdhi | mā vo riṣat kūṭagrāho mā va ā śāri lāṅgalam ||
english: Drive out, drive away; drive the cattle and acquire great wealth here; may the clutching trap not harm you, may the plough not splinter upon you.

sanskrit: mo asmākam ugrāḥ saṃrabdhās tanvaḥ kiṃ canāmamat | rāyaspoṣaṃ śunāsīrā atho sītābhagaś ca yaḥ ||
english: May no fierce, seized bodies of ours be harmed in anything whatsoever. O Śunāsīrā, increase of wealth — and also the fortune that belongs to the furrow.

sanskrit: deṣṭrī samudraḥ sinīvālī kṛṣiṃ no abhi hinvata | imā yāḥ pañca pradiśas tā vāto abhi hinvata | valīke satvatām iva tīvrā varṣantu vṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: The sea that appoints, Sinīvālī — may they two impel our ploughed field; these five directions here — may the wind impel them; like warriors on the battle-ground, let the rains rain fiercely.

sanskrit: śunaṃ kīnāśo anv etu vāhāñ chunaṃ phālo vinudann etu bhūmim | śunāsīrā haviṣā vāvṛdhānā śunaṃ dhānyāni kṛṇutāṃ yuvaṃ naḥ ||
english: Auspiciously let the ploughman follow the draft animals; auspiciously let the ploughshare go cleaving the earth; O Śunāsīrā, strengthened by the oblation, make our grains auspicious for us.

sanskrit: yā naḥ pīparad aśvinā jyotiṣmatī tamas tiraḥ | tām asme rāsetām iṣam ||
english: That which for us, O Aśvins, is luminous and pierces through the darkness — may you two bestow that nourishment upon us.
